threads.thread_goal: Align on overall hybrid course structure and weekly plan.

messages.text: Morning all, I have uploaded a first draft of the hybrid course outline to Hybrid Course Outline and Weekly Plan in our shared space, linked as A1. It covers weeks 1–12 with a focus on modes and learning outcomes, and should satisfy T1 at draft stage. For weeks 1–4 I have proposed: week 1 mostly on-site with a short online orientation, weeks 2–3 mixed, and week 4 more online to free lab space. Before we lock anything, can you skim A1 and flag if the weekly topics and the split between online and on-site feel realistic for your groups and lab access?

Thanks for sharing A1. I like the overall flow and the way you have aligned weekly outcomes with the programme map. One question: in week 1 you have both an on-site lab safety briefing and an online activity on study skills. Do you see those running in the same calendar week, or would the online piece open slightly earlier as a pre-arrival task? That might help students who need more time to process instructions.

Good point. My initial thought was to open the online study skills activity three days before the first on-site session, but I did not state that clearly in A1. If we agree, I can update T1 so week 1 explicitly shows a pre-week online component plus the on-site lab safety. Any objections to treating that as the pattern: online prep opening a few days before each on-site block?

I like the prep pattern. Looking at A1, weeks 2 and 3 currently have on-site labs plus online follow-up quizzes. For the first-year cohort, I would keep at least one structured on-site debrief in week 2 so they can ask questions about lab technique in person. Maybe we shift one of the online follow-ups in week 2 to an on-site small-group discussion and keep week 3 as written?

I have gone through the first four weeks in A1 with the lab timetable in mind. Week 4 being more online works for equipment maintenance, but we still need one short on-site slot that week for those who struggled with the earlier practicals. Could we mark week 4 as primarily online, with an optional on-site clinic session for lab skills?

I am fine with the overall structure in A1, but I am slightly unsure about how clearly the learning outcomes are phrased for week 1. Some of them read a bit broad, for example the one about engaging with hybrid learning. Could we tighten those so they are easier to explain to students on day one?

Agree on the wording. For week 1, maybe we phrase the outcome as: students can navigate the virtual learning environment, locate weekly tasks, and understand when they are expected on-site. That keeps it concrete and matches the hybrid focus in A1.

On weeks 2 and 3: I can adjust A1 so that week 2 has an on-site debrief after the lab, and the online quiz becomes a short in-class polling activity instead. Week 3 would then keep the online quiz and forum reflection as originally drafted. That still fits within T1 and the timetable constraints. Does that split feel balanced for the first four weeks?

Yes, that works for me. It keeps the early weeks more supported on-site while still building the habit of using the online space. For clarity, could we summarise the mode split for weeks 1–4 in A1 as a small table or list? That will help when we brief the programme coordinator.

If we add the optional on-site clinic in week 4, we should note in A1 that it is targeted at students who have flagged difficulties in earlier labs. That way we can coordinate with student support later and avoid overloading the timetable.

That suggested wording for week 1 outcomes sounds good to me. Could we also add one outcome about knowing where to find help, both in the virtual learning environment and on-site? That will link nicely to the later inclusion work.
Yes, I can draft that extra outcome and drop it into A1 later today, then you can all review the exact phrasing. I will keep it short and student-friendly.

I will add a simple summary list for weeks 1–4 in A1: week 1 pre-week online plus on-site induction, week 2 on-site lab plus on-site debrief, week 3 mixed with online quiz and forum, week 4 mainly online with an optional on-site clinic. Once that is in, I think we are close to being able to say the weekly structure and outcomes are agreed, unless anyone has major concerns.
No further concerns from me. The updated split for weeks 1–4 and the clarified outcomes look workable and align with the programme expectations I have seen.
Happy with this plan as well. The on-site and online balance in the first four weeks should support students who are new to labs and to the virtual learning environment.
Same here, I am comfortable moving forward on this basis. Once you have updated A1, we can share the outline with the programme coordinator for a quick check against the wider first-year structure.

Great, thanks all. I will make the agreed edits to A1 this afternoon and mark T1 as ready for coordinator review. To summarise: we are confirming the weekly structure and learning outcomes as per A1 with the tweaks discussed, and we are fixing the online versus on-site split for weeks 1–4 as described above.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize assessment plan, rubrics, and feedback approach.

messages.text: I have uploaded a draft assessment map and initial rubrics into Assessment Map and Rubrics Register, referenced as A2, and linked it to T2. The plan currently has three main components: a low-stakes online quiz series, a lab report, and a final applied project. Weightings are 20, 40, and 40 percent respectively. Could you review A2 and comment on whether the balance and timing feel right for first-year students in this hybrid format?

Looking at A2, I like the three-part structure. My only concern is that the first lab report deadline is currently in week 4, which might be tight given that week 4 is more online. Would it help to move that deadline to week 5 so we can use the week 4 online time to scaffold the report writing?

On the weightings in A2: 20 percent for the quiz series feels a bit high if they are mainly formative. Could we reduce that to 15 percent and add 5 percent for participation in online and on-site activities, using the attendance and engagement notes we will track later?

I like the idea of recognising participation, but I am a bit unsure how we would evidence it fairly across groups. Maybe we should first confirm the tracking process in A8 before we commit marks to it. For now, I am comfortable with the 20 percent quizzes if we keep them clearly aligned to the weekly outcomes.

From a lab perspective, the 40 percent lab report weighting in A2 makes sense, but I would like to see the rubric emphasise safe practice and accurate recording, not just the written discussion. Could we add a criterion for lab conduct and data integrity?

I am happy to move the first lab report deadline from week 4 to week 5 in A2. That will give us more time to model expectations in the virtual learning environment and in class. I will adjust the timeline in T2 accordingly.

On the quiz weighting: the programme handbook suggests at least one low-stakes component at 20 percent in first year, so I would prefer to keep the quizzes at 20 and not add a separate participation mark yet. We can still use participation data to trigger support without grading it. Does that address your concern?

Yes, that is fine. If the programme expects a 20 percent low-stakes component, I am comfortable keeping the quizzes at 20. Let us just make sure the quiz items map clearly to the weekly outcomes in A1 so they feel purposeful.

Agree on the lab conduct criterion. In A2, we could add a rubric row for safe practice and accurate data recording, worth maybe 20 percent of the lab report mark. That would still leave enough weight for analysis and discussion.
That breakdown works for me. It signals to students that how they work in the lab matters as much as what they write afterwards.

I will update the lab report rubric in A2 with that additional criterion and adjust the percentages. I will also double-check the final project rubric to ensure it captures teamwork and communication, since those are emphasised in the programme outcomes.

Switching to feedback: I have started a draft of Teaching Team Communication and Feedback Norms as A6, and I suggest we pair it with a comment bank under T10. My proposal is that we use a shared set of comments for common strengths and issues, and that we commit to returning feedback within two weeks for the lab report and one week for quizzes. Thoughts?

I like the turnaround times you suggest in A6. For the comment bank in T10, could we organise comments under the rubric criteria from A2, so that each criterion has a few positive and developmental examples? That will make it easier to stay consistent.

I am comfortable with the one-week turnaround for quizzes, but I might struggle with two weeks for the lab report if we get a large group. Could we phrase it in A6 as within two weeks, aiming for ten days where possible, so there is some flexibility?

Happy to help populate the comment bank for the lab-related criteria in T10. I can draft comments that speak to safe practice and accurate recording, using inclusive language so they are constructive rather than punitive.
Good point on workload. I will adjust A6 so the lab report feedback target reads as within two weeks, with an internal aim of around ten days. That should still meet quality assurance expectations.

To check we are aligned: we are keeping the three assessment components in A2 with weightings of 20 percent quizzes, 40 percent lab report, and 40 percent final project, with the first lab report deadline moved to week 5. We will use A6 and the T10 comment bank to standardise feedback, with one-week turnaround for quizzes and up to two weeks for the lab report. If everyone is happy with that, we can confirm the assessment plan and feedback approach.

That summary matches my understanding and fits with the programme requirements I have seen. I am happy to confirm the assessment types, weightings, deadlines, and the shared feedback standards and comment bank approach.

Great, I will finalise A2 and A6 with these details and send the assessment map to the programme coordinator for sign-off. I will also start structuring the T10 comment bank under the rubric headings so we can all add examples.

threads.thread_goal: Define inclusion strategies and support for learning difficulties.

messages.text: I have drafted an Inclusion and Learning Difficulties Support Guide as A3, linked to T5, focusing on adjustments we can realistically apply in this hybrid course. It covers things like alternative formats, extended time for certain tasks, and clear signposting of support. Could you read through A3 and suggest which practices we should treat as core for all groups, rather than optional extras?

Thanks for pulling A3 together. For me, core practices should include: providing slides and key resources in advance, using captions or transcripts for recorded materials, and having a consistent structure in the virtual learning environment so students know where to find things. Those feel essential rather than optional.

I agree with those. I would also add regular check-ins in weeks 2 and 4, as outlined in T11, as a core element. In A3 we could specify that each group runs a short structured check-in, either online or on-site, with a simple prompt to surface any difficulties early.

From the lab side, I think core practices should include offering written lab instructions alongside verbal briefings, and providing a quiet corner or alternative time for students who find the lab environment overwhelming. A3 mentions these, but we might want to mark them as standard rather than optional.

One thing I am not fully clear on in A3 is how we will coordinate with the student support officer when we notice concerns. T11 mentions a process for flagging at-risk students, but could we spell out in A3 who sends the initial email and what information we include, so we do not overload students with repeated contacts?

Good catch. I can update A3 so that the module lead sends the initial summary to the student support officer after the week 2 and week 4 check-ins, using a simple template from T11. Individual tutors can then follow up with students as needed, but the first contact with support will be coordinated.

That sounds workable. We should also note in A3 that we will anonymise any sensitive details in that initial summary and only share what is necessary for support planning, in line with institutional guidance.
On the week 2 and 4 check-ins in T11, could we agree that at least one of them is online? That might make it easier for students who find in-person discussions difficult to speak up.

For the quiet lab option, we will need to coordinate with timetabling, but I agree it should be a standard offer. Maybe we phrase it in A3 as: where feasible, a quieter lab slot or reduced group size will be offered for students who request it, and we will liaise with lab staff to arrange this.

On providing materials in advance, could we agree on a minimum timeframe? For example, slides and key resources uploaded to the virtual learning environment at least two working days before the session. That would give students with processing difficulties time to prepare.
I like the idea of one online check-in. I will update A3 and T11 so that week 2 is on-site and week 4 is online by default, unless a group has a specific reason to swap.
Two working days in advance for slides and key resources sounds reasonable and achievable. I will add that as a core expectation in A3, and we can echo it later in the operations guide.

To summarise what we seem to be calling core practices in A3: advance materials in accessible formats, consistent virtual learning environment structure, week 2 on-site and week 4 online check-ins from T11, coordinated contact with the student support officer, written lab instructions and a quieter lab option where feasible, and clear signposting of help routes. Are we comfortable naming these as the baseline for all groups?
Yes, that list reflects what I would expect as standard practice. It should make a real difference for students who find the transition to university challenging.
Agreed from me as well. Once A3 is updated, we should share it with the student support officer for a quick sense-check before we finalise T5 and T11.

Thanks all. I will revise A3 today to reflect these core practices and update T5 and T11 accordingly. We will then send the guide and the check-in plan to the student support officer for feedback. That will give us a clear, shared baseline for inclusion across all groups.

threads.thread_goal: Lock down VLE configuration, orientation module, and tracking processes.

messages.text: Quick update on the virtual learning environment: I have been working through the VLE Course Shell Configuration Checklist, A4, and the core structure is now in place for T4. Weekly modules for weeks 1–12 are created with placeholders, and the gradebook reflects the assessment plan from A2. I have also started a draft student orientation module based on A7 for T9. Could you take a look at the navigation and let me know if anything feels confusing from a student perspective?

I have clicked through the student view. Overall it is clear, but I wonder if we should move the orientation module, from A7, to the very top of the course menu and label it Start here, so new students do not miss it. At the moment it sits under Week 1, which might be less visible.

In the orientation module draft in A7, the low-stakes quiz currently focuses on general digital skills. Could we tweak it so that at least half the questions check understanding of this specific course structure, such as where to find weekly tasks and how attendance is recorded?

I noticed that announcements are currently only visible on the course home page. For students who mainly access the course via the mobile app, it might help to enable email notifications for key announcements, at least for the first few weeks. Is that covered in A4, or do we need to add it?

From a lab perspective, I like that each week has a Lab resources folder. Could we standardise the naming so that students always see Pre-lab, In-lab, and Post-lab materials in the same order? That might reduce confusion, especially for those juggling multiple modules.

Good suggestion. I can move the orientation module to the top of the menu and rename it Start here, while keeping a link in Week 1 as well. I will also update A4 so that this becomes part of our standard configuration checklist.

On the quiz in A7, yes, we can adjust the items so that at least half relate directly to this course: where to find weekly modules, how to submit assessments, and how attendance and participation are tracked. I will revise T9 accordingly.

Email notifications for announcements are not currently in A4, but we can add a step to enable them by default, with a note that students can change their own settings later. I will also check with IT support to confirm we are following institutional guidance before we finalise that step.

I like the Pre-lab, In-lab, Post-lab naming convention. It will also help when we prepare the week 1–4 materials under T3. Could we add that structure to A4 so it is applied consistently across all lab weeks?
Yes, that would be ideal. I can help populate the Pre-lab sections for the first four weeks once T3 is underway, so students always see a familiar pattern when they open a lab week.

On attendance and participation tracking: I have reviewed the Attendance and Participation Tracking Template, A8, linked to T8. It currently has separate tabs for on-site and online sessions. To keep things simple, could we merge these into one sheet with a column indicating mode, so we can see a full picture of each student at a glance?
I support merging the tabs in A8. It will also make it easier to spot patterns, such as students who attend on-site but rarely engage online, or the other way around.

For T8, we also need to agree on a simple participation indicator. I suggest we use a three-point scale each week: engaged, partially engaged, and limited engagement, based on a quick review of attendance and activity logs. We can record that in A8 and use it to trigger early support rather than for grading.

I like the three-point scale idea. We should document the definitions in A8 so that we apply them consistently. For example, engaged might mean attended and completed most weekly tasks, while limited engagement might mean missed sessions and little online activity.

Agreed. I will update A8 to merge the tabs and add the three-point participation scale with clear descriptors. I will also run a quick mock session in the virtual learning environment to test the process for T8 before we rely on it in week 1.

To check we are ready to sign off: the VLE shell now has weekly modules, a gradebook aligned with A2, announcements configured with email notifications, and a Start here orientation module with a course-specific quiz from A7. Attendance and participation will be tracked using the updated A8 template and the three-point scale under T8. Are we comfortable approving this structure and tracking method for launch?
Yes, the structure looks clear from a student and lab perspective, especially with the consistent Pre-lab, In-lab, Post-lab folders. I am happy to approve the navigation and tracking approach.
Agreed from me as well. Once the mock session for T8 confirms everything works as expected, we can consider the VLE structure and tracking method approved for this run of the course.

threads.thread_goal: Align on hybrid lab/practical procedures and team operations guide.

messages.text: I have uploaded a draft of the Hybrid Lab and Practical Session Procedures as A5, linked to T6, and a first version of the Teaching Team Communication and Feedback Norms as A6 feeding into T7 and T12. A5 covers safety, preparation, remote alternatives, and a supervision checklist. A6 pulls together our norms on communication, feedback, and inclusion. Could you review both and flag anything that feels unclear or unrealistic for your groups?

Thanks for pulling A5 and A6 together. In A5, the remote alternative for labs suggests using pre-recorded videos plus a data set. Could we add a short reflective prompt as a required element, so students who cannot attend in person still engage actively rather than just watching?

In A6, the communication norms mention using the channel for general queries and email for personal matters, which I support. Could we also specify expected response times for student messages, for example within two working days, so we are consistent across groups?

I like the supervision checklist in A5. One thing I am not sure about is how we record near misses in the lab. The checklist mentions logging them, but not where. Should we add a shared form or a simple log in our team space, so we can spot patterns and adjust teaching?

On A6, I appreciate the section on inclusive language in feedback. Could we add one or two concrete examples of how to rephrase common comments, for instance turning vague phrases into specific, actionable suggestions? That might help colleagues who are less used to this style.

Good idea. I will update A5 so that the remote alternative always includes a short reflective task, such as explaining how they would adjust the procedure if given different equipment. That will be part of T6.

On response times, yes, we can add to A6 that we aim to respond to student messages within two working days, and that urgent issues should be flagged in the subject line. I will also note that we will use the channel for teaching team coordination and keep student queries in the official platforms.

For near misses, I suggest we add a simple shared log in our team space, referenced in A5 and T6, where lab staff can record date, activity, and a brief note. We can then review this log mid-semester to see if any procedures need adjusting.

On the feedback examples in A6 and T10, I can draft a few pairs of comments, such as replacing unclear phrases with more specific ones, and add them to the comment bank. That should make it easier for everyone to adopt the same tone.

Looking at T12, the operations guide will need to bring together A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, and A8. It might help if we structure it around the student journey: before week 1, weekly teaching, assessments, labs, and support. That way new colleagues can quickly see what to do at each stage.
I like that structure. I am happy to help with the weekly teaching section of T12, summarising how we use the virtual learning environment, attendance tracking from A8, and feedback norms from A6.
I can take a pass at the support section of T12, drawing on A3 and T11, so that the guide clearly explains how we run check-ins and when we contact the student support officer.

Great, I will focus on the labs and practicals section of T12, using A5 and the near-miss log process we discussed. Once we have a full draft, we can ask two colleagues outside this group to review it for clarity.

To check we are ready to sign off: A5 now sets out standard lab procedures, including remote alternatives with reflection, written instructions, quieter lab options where feasible, and a near-miss log. A6 and the related T7 norms define our communication channels, response times, feedback turnaround, and examples of constructive comments. T12 will consolidate these into an operations guide structured around the student journey. Are we comfortable approving A5 and the overall operations approach for this course run?
Yes, that summary matches my understanding. I am happy to sign off on the lab procedures in A5 and the consolidated operations approach feeding into T12.

Agreed. I will finalise A5 and A6 with the changes discussed and then pull everything into the T12 operations guide draft. Once we have external feedback, we can store the final version in the shared drive and link it in the virtual learning environment.
